title: QBR KPI scenario playbook and sample tables
content:
Purpose: quick, scenario-driven reference for QBR owners that defines the core operational KPIs we present to customers (latency, uptime, cost/token, cache hit rate), shows measurement recipes, and includes ready-to-copy sample tables and talking points.

Audience: CSMs and CS analysts preparing renewal QBR decks; engineering partners for sanity-checking calc methods.

Key idea: move away from one-size-fits-all KPI pages. Use scenario rows (steady-state, peak-event, regression signal) so customers see how metrics behave under different workload shapes.

METRIC DEFINITIONS & MEASUREMENT RECIPES (practical, with edge cases)

1) P95 tail latency (user-visible generation latency)
Definition: the 95th percentile of end-to-end request latency for generation calls in the measurement window. End-to-end = request received by Redwood -> first final token returned to client.
Why use P95: captures tail impact for interactive apps; less noisy than P99 while still picking up regressions.
Measurement recipe (SQL-ish):
  SELECT
    percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) AS p95_ms
  FROM inference_requests
  WHERE model_family = 'customer-default'
    AND status = '200'
    AND timestamp >= '{{start}}' AND timestamp < '{{end}}'
Notes / edge cases:
  - Exclude streaming partial tokens (measure finalization time only) unless customer relies on streaming UX — then compute streaming P95 separately (time to first token).
  - Drop synthetic health-check calls by filtering client_id / route tags.
  - For multi-model fallbacks, annotate rows by served_model and include fallback-rate column.

2) Uptime (availability to customer)
Definition: percent of 1-minute intervals in the window where customer-visible success rate >= 99% (success = non-5xx on inference calls and console heartbeats).
Why this formulation: reduces noise from single-request blips; aligns with SLO-style reporting.
Measurement recipe:
  For each minute in window, compute success_rate = successful_requests / total_requests. Uptime = 100 * (count(minutes with success_rate >= 0.99) / total_minutes).
Notes:
  - If customer uses dedicated capacity, split hosted vs. dedicated in the table.
  - For private deployments, use agent heartbeats + app-level checks; note that agent metrics might lag by ~30s.

3) Cost per token (unit economics)
Definition: total platform cost allocated to the customer’s inference traffic divided by total tokens generated (input+output) in the window.
Calculation recipe (high-level):
  cost_per_token = (gpu_compute_cost + storage_cost*share + infra_overhead) / total_tokens
  - gpu_compute_cost: estimated by GPU-minutes * model_profile_gpu_rate
  - infra_overhead: small fixed portion for orchestration/egress (configurable)
Notes:
  - Display both raw cost/token and normalized cost/token (adjusted for batching and caching) to show how configuration changes matter.
  - For multi-tier pricing, show both platform internal cost (for engineering) and billed price (for customer-facing economics).
  - When tokens are very low, prefer cost per 1k tokens to avoid tiny decimals.

4) Cache hit rate (prefix/KV cache effectiveness)
Definition: fraction of requests where the runtime served from cache (prefix or KV) such that expensive model compute was avoided.
Formula: cache_hit_rate = cached_requests / eligible_requests.
Measurement recipe notes:
  - eligible_requests: requests for which cache key was present (i.e., same prompt prefix length/route) — exclude dynamic tool-calls or long multi-tool ops that aren’t cached.
  - Provide both prefix_cache_hit and kv_cache_hit if both are enabled.
  - Important to show cache savings: cost_savings_estimate = cache_hit_rate * average_compute_cost_per_request.

SAMPLE KPI TABLES (copyable CSV rows)
Table A: Customer QBR summary (scenario rows)\Columns: scenario, window_start, window_end, p95_ms, uptime_pct, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, cache_hit_pct, notes\Rows (example):
steady-state,2025-06-01,2025-06-30,210,99.7,0.85,42,normal traffic, stable model v3
peak-event,2025-06-20,2025-06-21,480,98.2,1.40,29,marketing campaign peak, autoscale reached cap
regression-signal,2025-05-09,2025-05-10,920,95.5,2.10,11,model rollback caused longer decode times

Table B: Raw weekly cadence (example rows for ingestion into spreadsheet)\Columns: week_of, requests, successful_requests, p95_ms, p50_ms, uptime_pct, tokens_total, billed_cost_usd, platform_cost_usd, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, cache_hits, cache_eligible, cache_hit_pct\Rows (sample):
2025-07-06,1,230,000,1,224,000,210,102,99.7,45,320, $3,800, $1,680, 37.2, 18,900, 49,000, 38.6
2025-07-13,1,450,000,1,445,000,230,118,99.4,56,420, $5,430, $2,010, 35.6, 20,050, 56,600, 35.4

Calculations to include in QBR deck (suggested visuals)\  - Small multiple: p95_ms over last 12 weeks (line chart) with vertical lines for releases/rollouts.
  - Stacked bar: cost breakdown (GPU vs infra vs egress) per month.
  - Scatter: cache_hit_pct vs cost_per_1k_tokens (each point = week) showing correlation.

ALERT & TALKING POINT THRESHOLDS (suggested defaults)
  - p95 regression: > 2x baseline p95 for 3 consecutive days => notify eng and CSM.
  - uptime: drop below 99% in any 24-hour window => incident review and customer comms.
  - cost per 1k tokens: increase > 30% QoQ with no traffic pattern change => flag for cost regression analysis.
  - cache hit rate: sudden drop > 15 percentage points week-over-week => inspect cache keys, prompt drift, or rollout fallout.

SCENARIO ANNOTATIONS (how to explain to customers)
  - Steady-state: show p95, uptime, cost/token, cache hit trend. Highlight optimizations applied (batching, caching, quantization).
  - Peak-event: explain autoscale behavior, throttling/backpressure, and tradeoffs of latency vs. cost during the event. Include back-of-envelope: delta-cost = (burst_tokens * avg_cost_token_peak) - baseline.
  - Regression: provide RCA summary: what changed (model version, kernel changes, infra), mitigation steps (rollback, tuning), residual risk.

PRE-QBR DATA PULL CHECKLIST (CS analyst)
  - Pull last 90 days of inference_requests aggregated by minute (fields: timestamp_minute, requests, successes, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, served_model, route).
  - Export cache logs for same window with keys: request_id, cache_hit, cache_type, key_namespace.
  - Get billing invoice lines & internal cost allocation for the customer’s workload.
  - Map recent rollouts (tags) to the time axis: release_id, rollout_pct, start, end.
  - Confirm with Solutions Eng whether any private deployments need separate reporting.

QBR SLIDES — SLIDE-BY-SLIDE MICRO SCRIPT (short)\ 1) One-line health verdict (green/yellow/red) + 30s summary.\ 2) Top KPI snapshot (Table A row for the most recent month).\ 3) Trend visuals (p95 and cost lines).\ 4) Recent incidents or regressions + status.\ 5) Action items and asks (resources, CS experiments, config tweaks).

COMMUNICATION TEMPLATES (snippets)\  - Pre-QBR note to customer: "Sharing our draft KPI snapshot and the data we plan to review. Please flag any additional metrics to include."\  - Post-QBR action summary: bullet list of items with owners and due dates.

OPEN QUESTIONS / WORK IN PROGRESS\  - How to best attribute cross-customer shared-gpu overhead in cost_per_token (proposal: 10% infra pooling markup; needs FP sign-off).\  - Standardize streaming-first-token vs final-token latency naming in decks (different customers ask for different things).\  - Automate scenario row generation in the QBR automation pipeline (CS-automation spike planned Q3).

NEXT STEPS\  - Iterate on these CSV templates; CS analysts to test with three mid-market customer datasets.\  - Add a regression RCA template linked to each scenario row (id + summary + patch/rollback link).

NOTES TO SELF (Priya):\  - Keep the p95 vs p50 contrast in the main slide — product teams love seeing skew.\  - Save a copy of weekly raw table as "qbr-weekly-raw-{customer}-{yyyy-mm-dd}.csv" in shared drive before trimming.

Appendix: example SQL snippets (for analytics team)\  - compute p95 per day:
      SELECT date_trunc('day', timestamp) as day,
             percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p95_ms
      FROM inference_requests
      WHERE customer_id = 'acme-corp' AND timestamp >= '2025-05-01'
      GROUP BY day
  - compute cache hit rate weekly:
      SELECT date_trunc('week', ts) as week,
             sum(case when cache_hit then 1 else 0 end)::float / sum(1) as cache_hit_pct
      FROM cache_events
      WHERE customer_id = 'acme-corp' AND ts >= '2025-05-01'
      GROUP BY week

End of doc.
